title: Mass funeral in Gaza after bodies recovered of more than 100 people killed in 2023 Israeli strike
description:
(4 Aug 2026) 
FOR CLEAN VERSION SEE STORY NUMBER: 4676588

++THUMBNAIL:
Palestinians carry the flag-draped bodies of members of the Hassayna and Abu Sharia families, who were killed in an Israeli strike in 2023 and whose remains were recently recovered from the rubble, during their funeral in Gaza City, Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Jehad Alshrafi; ID 26216390674120)++

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 4 August 2026
1. Various of people gathering near bodies wrapped in Palestinian flags
2. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Taysir al-Hassayna, relative of victims:
++PARTIALLY COVERED++
"We were subjected to a horrific massacre on November 22, 2023, in which more than 300 martyrs perished in a gruesome massacre witnessed by the unjust world. The only crime of these martyrs was that they remained steadfast and resilient in their homes, believing that these homes would protect them from the brutality and crimes of the Israeli occupation. But they were taken by surprise when nine incendiary missiles struck the very place where they were, and they all perished. Not one of them survived. Three years after this horrific massacre, we were only able to recover the bodies of 112 martyrs out of more than 300. More than two-thirds remain buried under the rubble, their blood, bones, and flesh mingled with the concrete blocks, leaving no trace, as if their bodies had evaporated without a trace.”
3. Pan from destroyed area to wrapped bodies on ground
4. Various of bodies wrapped in Palestinian flags with photos of victims
5. Various of people offering funeral prayers for victims and procession
6. Wide of bodies wrapped in Palestinian flags
7. Various of people carrying bodies wrapped in Palestinian flags, marching through streets of Gaza City
STORYLINE:
Palestinians gathered on Tuesday for a mass funeral of more than 100 bodies finally recovered from a deadly Israeli strike in Gaza in 2023.

More than 300 people were killed on November 22, 2023, weeks into the war with Hamas, when warplanes flattened a residential block in Gaza City’s Sabra neighborhood.

Around 40 bodies were recovered soon afterward in a frantic scramble of rough tools and bare hands, but most were buried deep beneath the rubble.

Reports of the high number of victims in one of the war's deadliest attacks took days to reach the public in the chaos just before its first ceasefire.

Over the weekend, first responders dug through the destroyed buildings and recovered remains of 112 victims, including 40 children, according to the Civil Defense, a rescue agency operating under the Hamas-run Interior Ministry.

It said 157 bodies still have not been found.

“The only crime of these martyrs was that they remained steadfast and resilient in their homes, believing that these homes would protect them,” one relative, Taysir al-Hassayna, told The Associated Press following the funeral prayers.

On Tuesday, the remains of the victims, wrapped in Palestinian flags, were laid in rows on the ground.

Many were marked with photos, and flower petals were scattered around all. 

Hundreds of people surrounded the bodies for funeral prayers, some standing on the rubble.

Following the prayers, people carried the bodies on stretchers along a narrow street lined by destroyed buildings and buried them in a nearby cemetery.

Only now are some bodies of people killed in the war's ferocious early months slowly being recovered, as a fragile ceasefire that took effect in October allows such efforts to push ahead in parts of devastated Gaza.

Those discoveries have contributed to the war's rising toll.
